(i) reducing spectral accuracy in the spectral transform is a promising way to improve forecast efficiency in high-resolution NWP and (ii) the ratio between the gridpoint resolution and the spectral resolution is an important parameter that can be adjusted to improve forecast efficiency.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the question of whether the current approach of increasing resolution by a factor 2 every 8 years is a viable and cost-effective approach to improve weather and climate prediction, or whether a more judicious approach should be considered.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

there is a need for a deeper understanding of uncertainty in high-resolution simulations and that the current approach is to explore and understand the sensitivity to uncertainty for each part of the NWP model.
increasing resolution by a factor 2 every 8 years is an illusion and that the panacea lies in a more judicious choice of the resolution ratio in spectral space.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the formal accuracy in the spectral transforms is not the limiting factor for NWP simulations, while a reduction of the ratio between the horizontal resolutions in gridpoint versus wavenumber space may be beneficial.
, in order to increase forecast accuracy, the model should be tuned for a given resolution and that this tuning should be performed with a focus on the forecast error.
the formal accuracy of the spectral transforms and the horizontal resolution in spectral and gridpoint space are not independent.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ratio of the horizontal resolution in spectral and gridpoint space is a critical model parameter, which should not be set to unity.
the ratio between gridpoints and wavenumbers should be kept constant, even if the formal accuracy of the spectral transforms is reduced.

the ratio of gridpoint resolution to the spectral truncation is not a constant but depends on the model resolution and the spectral truncation, and should not be set to the same value as in low-resolution models.
